title: Model enums as exact allowed-set matches that reject anything else, and namespace your helper functions
summary: When a parameter must be one of a few values, encode the allowed set and reject the rest, rather than letting an unlisted string fall through to a default that hides the mistake. Keep related functions discoverable with a shared prefix and a clear public/private boundary, and declare locals up front.
technique: A case that matches the exact allowed words and otherwise returns an error; a small canonicalizing function that maps synonyms and returns a failure code for anything it does not know; function names prefixed by a domain (public) or with a leading underscore (private), e.g. a plugin facade with the same entry points in every file.
evidence_note: bin/queue-vcs-probe:41-50 normal_type() returns a canonical name or `return 1`; the caller rejects an empty canonical as unknown (lines 83-84). It also uses ${TYPE^^} style normalization before matching. assets.d/* plugins all expose the shared queue_asset_facilities/hints/check_* facade; private helpers are _queue_asset_*.
invariants: Model a small closed set as an explicit match that returns an error for everything outside it.
Do not let an unknown enum silently become a default; surface it as unknown.
Namespace private helpers with a domain prefix and a leading underscore to signal intent; keep a stable public facade.
Always declare function-local variables with local so they cannot leak into the caller's namespace.
